audit.why: 50.34% over 2370 games is a true even lane. The packet levelChart (Skill/Zaahen/Zaahen/Skill/Skill/Zaahen/Zaahen) matches both phases[].side and win[] exactly, so no chart flip is needed and no full/content disagreement exists. Difficulty 6/10 and EVEN are consistent with the win rate.
audit.corrected: No change. Chart verified consistent across both layers and against the packet.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 text calls World Ender a 'reset' and implies it restores him. Riot's text says World Ender fears nearby minions and grants AD, increased healing and Move Speed, and that a takedown EXTENDS the effect. It does not revive or reset him. The mirror audit made the same correction from Aatrox's side (revive belongs to Zaahen's passive).
audit.why: A player told Aatrox 'resets' at 6 will disengage a won fight expecting a second life bar. The real spike is a 120/100/80s timed stat window you can outlast.
audit.corrected: whys[4] and spikes[1].text restated as a timed stat swing extended by takedowns, with the 120s rank-1 cooldown made explicit; wants.foe[2] reworded from 'reset-fuelled' to the extension.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive kit interaction of this matchup was nowhere on the page: Infernal Chains (W) applies grounding, and Zaahen's E is a dash. Nothing in full or content told the player his escape is turned off by the chain. Also missing: Deathbringer Stance (P) is an auto-attack reset, so the burst tell is the wind-up, not an ability cast.
audit.why: Zaahen's only repositioning tool is the E dash (10/9.5/9/8.5/8s). Aatrox's W grounds and then drags the target back to the centre, so dashing out mid-chain both fails and wastes the cooldown. This is the single interaction that decides who wins an extended trade.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now names Infernal Chains, its 16s rank-3 cooldown and the grounding rule; breakdown.mid tells the player to hold E until the chain expires; report[5].t now carries the Deathbringer Stance auto-reset tell; wants.foe[1] names Umbral Dash and its 9s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cooldowns were referenced only by name ('track The Darkin Blade') with no numbers anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: The Darkin Blade is 14/12/10/8/6s and Infernal Chains 20/18/16/14/12s. Real numbers make the trade window concrete instead of a slogan.
audit.corrected: 10s (Q at rank 3) and 16s (W at rank 3) written into breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.mid and dosFull[0].d.

audit.why: Anti-heal is already core in report[8] and breakdown.late, which is what the needs-antiheal missing-interaction asks for (Deathbringer Stance, Umbral Dash passive and World Ender all heal).

audit.whatIsWrong: Zaahen's own ability names are inconsistent between layers and cannot be verified from Data Dragon.
audit.why: content calls W 'Ominous Return' while the mirror audit calls the same pull 'Dreaded Return'. Zaahen is not in the kit files by name, so neither can be confirmed.
audit.corrected: Left alone; recorded in questionsForUser and unverified rather than guessed.

edits.before: Both ults arrive and it flattens out. Aatrox's World Ender gives him a huge stat swing plus reset threat, so your R Final Retribution has to be saved as an anti-engage answer rather than a first-blood button — don't ult into his ult.
edits.after: Both ults arrive and it flattens out. World Ender is a 120-second stat swing that only extends on a takedown — it never revives him, so weather the timer rather than trading into it. Save your R as the answer to his commit, not a first-blood button.

edits.before: At 6 it's even — Aatrox's World Ender stat swing and resets cancel your lane lead.
edits.after: At 6 it's even — World Ender's stat swing extends on takedowns and outlasts your R.

edits.before: From 3 to 5 you own the lane: dodge Aatrox's Q sweet spots, punish the long cooldown with your Q and E, and he can only heal off good casts you deny. At 6 World Ender neutralizes the edge, so hold your R defensively.
edits.after: From 3 to 5 you own the lane: dodge Aatrox's Q sweet spots and punish the cooldown — 10s at rank 3. Infernal Chains grounds you, so hold your E dash until the chain expires or you are dragged back in. At 6, hold R defensively.
